- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.text:
This repo (Memos/Slash-like note app, Go backend + React frontend) has no Redis dependency anywhere — no `redis` import, package, or config exists in the codebase. The "cache" hits found are unrelated: a client-side `cacheService.ts` for the memo editor draft cache, and TanStack Query's in-memory `query-client.ts` cache, both of which run entirely in the browser with no external cache server.

r01.
Premise correction: there is no Redis connection or Redis-backed cache layer in this repository — I searched for `redis` across the entire codebase (Go backend, proto files, and web frontend) and found zero matches.

Actual mechanism: caching here is done client-side in the React app, not via Redis:
- `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/cacheService.ts` — an in-browser draft cache for the memo editor (keyed by memo, stored client-side, no server round-trip).
- `/bench/repo/web/src/lib/query-client.ts` — the TanStack Query client instance, which provides in-memory query caching for API responses in the browser.

Neither of these is a "user entries" cache with a Redis-style TTL — TanStack Query has its own `staleTime`/`gcTime` config (worth checking `query-client.ts` directly if you need those values), but there's no server-side Redis cache or TTL for user records. If you're looking for a specific TTL on user data, it doesn't exist in this codebase as of the current `main` branch (commit `2d01420`).
